I’ve played hundreds of hours of Red Alert 3 outside of Steam. While I consider Red Alert 2: Yuri’s Revenge to be the best Red Alert game. Red Alert 3 is a very good sequel and the Uprising expansion was a very fun campaign. The game’s scale is much smaller than RA2’s, but it introduces significant, new mechanics that leads to interesting strategies and tactics. The game introduces something like hero abilities from games like League of Legends or Warcraft 3. The game greatly improved naval combat, which I considered a bit lackluster in the predecessors. The co-op design in the game’s campaign is awesome and something I wish other RTS games implement. The AI is very competent and the game’s content is vast. The campaigns are well done and there’s diversity in the factions. Like most of the C&C games, Red Alert 3 has a healthy modding community that provides further content and fun. Command and Conquer does it again with another great installment onto the Red Alert series. Although not as good as its predecessor C&C: RA3 continues to offer no need for builders and no worry of controlling population. 

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
Unlike past Red Alerts I only played about one skirmish as I did not find the AI as enjoyable as the predecessors. This Red Alert offers some interesting new teams and resource harvesting concepts which seem different than before. Like in the past Red Alert games the Russians and Allies are pretty much the same basic strategy type, while the third team offers a fresh new tactics. Similar to past Red Alerts to expand bases (when playing as either Allies or Soviets) you can build Mobile Construction Vehicles. But, unlike past Red alerts they have also added the ability for Prospectors (allied ore miners) to deploy into Command Centers which allow you to expand to nearby areas mitigating large costs. The USSR can build “Sputnik” which can also deploy into a command center. Both of these units allow for cheaper base expansion. This is different for the Japanese whose buildings are built by transforming vehicles into buildings and thus are not limited to base parameters.
 
[b]Campaign:[/b]
The campaign took me about 21 hours to complete (that includes Allies, Russians, and Rising Sun missions). Interestingly the campaigns intertwine and in some instances you play the same missions but just as the opposing team, which I sort of liked. In the case of this game the missions are not exactly gripping, but that is the case with all strategy games. The campaign offers a great composition of actors which make you laugh, gasp, and reminisce in the old days when you first sat down and played Red Alert. Some of the missions are very quick and last no time at all while others can last a couple hours. 

[b]Results:[/b]
If you are expecting something just like the second Red Alert then you will be disappointed. There is only one Yuri and his revenge was an epic adventure that could only be told once. If you are interested in playing a strategy game that brings Red Alert on a new adventure then this is a game worth checking out. With an amazing intro song to boot and epic campaign cut scenes that you won't forget. Red Alert 3 really takes Westwood’s dream into action: hot babes who flirt with you throughout your entire game and keep your spirits bolstered with cheesy lines. 

Pros:
+Great campaign with fun dialogue and amazing cut scenes.
+New Empire of the Rising Sun team which brings all new tactics to the game
+Campaign missions that don't just require you to continually build a base over and over again, but rather test you through a variety of scenarios.
+Epic main menu music that just makes you want to jump right into the Russian campaign. 
+It has been 18 years and Tanya still hasn't aged over 30... a mystery? Or did someone use the chronosphere?

Cons:
-Its not Red Alert 2 (that game already existed, if you want that game you may want to go find the disk from your shelf)
-Some campaign missions can run rather long, while others last about 10 minutes. (Some missions took me up to three hours). 
-Poor movement AI can cause units to not exactly act how you want them too.

[h1]TL:DR? See Conclusion[/h1]

[h1]NOTE:[/h1] I have played this game extensively, but not on Steam.

[h1]INTRODUCTION:[/h1]
Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3 is a Real Time Strategy (RTS) game serving as the third installment of the popular Command & Conquer series.  It features a rebooted story and a brand new faction called 'The Empire of the Rising Sun'.  However, unlike its predecessors,  Electronic Arts who acquired Westwood Studios, the original developers of the game, produced Red Alert 3.  It is one of the last few remaining franchises who use live action cutscenes which the series is known for.

Players once again take the role of the unknown commander who leads either the Allied Forces, the Soviet Army, or the newly resurrected Imperial Armed Forces to ultimate victory.

Red Alert 3's story starts with the Soviet Union in complete collapse after the events of Red Alert 2.  In an effort to stop the USSR's defeat, surviving Soviet leaders use a time machine to go back in history and erase Albert Einstein in order to prevent him from developing Allied technology.  Upon returning to the Present day however, they discover that without Einstein, nuclear technology was  never developed.  With this turn of events, this meant that the US never bombed Japan and the Empire never surrendered during World War 2.  Now the Empire has risen once more and poses a new threat to both the Soviets and the Allies prompting the hilarious line by actor Peter Stormare as Dr. Gregor Zelinsky: “We now have...two mortal enemies?” 

[h1]PROS:[/h1]
+ Colorful visuals and very nice graphics with good use of Physx technology
+ New 'Empire of the Rising Sun' faction is fun to play featuring highly advanced, extremely versatile, very expensive, and unhealthily suicidal units (ex. Tsunami Tank:[i] “HA! Give us a good death” [/i] Imperial Warrior: [I] “Death before defeat!”[/i] Shogun Battleship: [I] “Ramming speed!”[/i] Yari Sub: [I] “We're taking you with us!” [/i]
+ Fun campaign for all 3 factions
+ Hilarious, Hammy, Cheesy but overall good voice acting
+ Humorous and entertaining Tutorial
+ All units for all factions now have secondary abilities
+ Co-op campaign
+ Very nice Music and Sounds

[h1]CONS:[/h1]
- The very colorful art-style that could cause headaches for some people
- Some low polygon models, low resolution shadows, and poor textures can be seen here and there
- Short campaign for each faction
- Story is shallow and uses way to many cliche elements from the previous Red Alert 2
- Occasional pathfinding problems
- Balance issues with some of the units
- Some outstanding bugs that was never fixed (for some reason, changing the graphics quality and  resolution at the same time MAY cause a crash)
- Despite EA's vast resources and use of big name actors like Peter Stormare and George Takei, I can't help but feel that they were not able to live up to the standard of Westwood.
- Broken multiplayer on Steam (No idea if it works in Origin)

[h1]CONCLUSION:[/h1]
GREAT RTS GAME.  Although it does not fully capture the magic of Red Alert 2, Red Alert 3 still delivers a great fast paced experience for RTS fans looking for a quick fix.  The campaign is fun with a story that is easy to follow but uses a lot of cliche plot elements.  The Soundtrack is excellent and the over-the-top, hammy, and cheesy voice acting are very entertaining.  Multiplayer is also fun if you're looking for a casual RTS experience since the AI does pose a challenge on higher difficulties.  In addition, new game mechanics such as the secondary abilities and the new faction spices up the action.

Now we come on whether or not I recommend this game.  If you're in this for the single player experience, sure I can RECOMMEND this game easily.  If you're in this for the multiplayer experience, I DO NOT RECOMMEND this game here on Steam because for some reason the Servers are broken so you're better off purchasing this in EA's Origin Platform.

[h1]Introduction[/h1]
[b]Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3[/b] is the first entry in the [b]Red Alert[/b] series made by a different studio. In the previous expansion for [b]Red Alert 2[/b], the series introduced a bit more over the top story and units you control. This entry continues in this legacy and presents a humorous story with real actors, as well as unique and interesting units for each faction.

[h1]Single-player[/h1]
The single-player offers three campaigns for the Soviet Union, the United States of America, and the Empire of the Rising Sun. It takes about 20 hours to complete them all on the highest difficulty setting. There is no restriction, so you can start playing as any nation you want. The great addition is that you can play all three campaigns in a co-op with a friend or random player. You receive an AI partner if you choose to play alone. Other than that, you can play Skirmish against the AI on several maps.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2155298139
[h3]Story[/h3]
The Soviet Union is almost at its downfall, and only last hope remains. The Soviet Premier manages to travel in time, kills [i]Albert Einstein[/i], and returns. Without [i]Einstein[/i], the western Allies have never gotten an advantage over the Soviets. However, the happiness of the Soviet leadership will not last long, as the new threat from the East emerges. [i]The Empire of the Rising Sun[/i] (Japan) simultaneously invades both Americans and the Soviets. Without [i]Einstein’s[/i] scientific research, Japan was never bombed with nuclear weapons, as those do not exist anymore. All three factions are now in a war with everyone, and it is up to you, which one will you lead to a victory.
[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
The gameplay’s core is the same for every faction. You collect golden ore from mines which serve as money and build powerplants to keep the power going in your base. Without electricity power, most of your buildings stop working, especially the turrets for your defense. The great addition is that you can build almost every building both on the ground and on water. This allows for more diverse base-building than in previous games. You expand and build new bases anywhere you want, but the ore mines placement is always the same.

The base building is almost the same for every faction, as you always need to build powerplants, barracks, dockyards, defensive turrets, and more. They have a few noticeable gameplay differences, but you will not be completely lost when you will start playing as another nation. The main differences come with the units. There are always anti-infantry, anti-vehicle, and anti-air units. The game has four different unit branches: infantry, ground vehicles, ships, and aircraft. They all differ in each faction, and every single one has two abilities. For example, [i]Soviet Conscript[/i] has an assault rifle and an ability to throw Molotov’s cocktails. The [i]American Peacekeeper[/i] has armour, short-range shotgun, and can equip a shield. Lastly, the [i]Imperial Warrior[/i] has a rifle and sword, which increases his overall speed. The same goes for all the units in the game. Every nation has something that counters the other’s units and abilities. Nations also differ with their unique ability tree. While the Soviets can throw satellites on their foes, Americans can freeze them, and the Japanese can send their kamikaze squadrons.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2155296739
Unfortunately, the AI is not the brightest, as it is very scripted in the campaign. It does very rarely something on its own, and once you manage to damage their income or destroy their recruitment buildings, you won. In most cases, the AI will not try to repair their buildings or even build new ones. It does not even try to counter your units, so you can easily spam them with one unit type if you manage to hit them quickly and precisely. The AI is a bit better in the Skirmish, as it is trying to do something, but do not expect an enormous challenge, as you will not find it there.

Another negative is that some campaign missions, especially the ones where you mostly control just heroes, are tiresome. The strength in this game is to build what you want, and that is gone when you are restricted to play with just one or a few units.

[h1]Multi-player[/h1]
The official servers are down, but the option to play [b]Red Alert 3[/b] online, as well as other [b]Command & Conquer[/b] games is still there.

[url=https://cnc-online.net/en/][quote]All you need to do to play [b]Command & Conquer[/b] games online is to go to [b]cnc-online[/b], register yourself, download a launcher, and follow the instructions.[/quote][/url]

The multi-player offers the aforementioned Skirmish maps against real players. There are various maps from 1v1 up to 3v3. Playing against players is definitely a better option, as you have to use accordingly faction’s units and abilities. Everything else works the same as in the single-player.

[h1]Audiovisuals[/h1]
The game’s art style is something that I really adore, as it is quite unique and colourful. All three factions are very diverse with their distinctive appearance. You can easily recognize every unit by their looks and can exactly expect what they can do. Some of the visual effects look great for a game from 2008, and that especially applies to some visual effects and water.

However, [b]Command & Conquer[/b] series was always known for presenting real actors in its cutscenes. The Soviet premier is played by famous [i]Tim Curry[/i], who wants to spread Communism to the whole world and Space. Against him stands anti-communists presidents of the United States, portrayed by [i]J.K. Simmons[/i], and they are all invaded by the Japanese Emperor, played by [i]George Takei[/i]. There are, of course, way more actors and actresses, and from some from cutscenes, you can clearly see that they are trying to hold their laugh. When talking about actors, one must mention quotes of the units, as every unit has their quotes depending on the situation they are currently in. Sometimes they are really hilarious or cheesy.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2155296869
The sound effects of all the weaponry, machinery, and explosions are just great, but what really stands out is the soundtrack, which is a mix of several genres, mostly industrial metal with presented vocals. The third version of [i]Hell March[/i] is present. Every faction has their own compositions, and when you are in the middle of a chaotic battle, it all clicks together.

[h1] Performance[/h1]
The game was tested with an [b]i5 8300H, GTX 1060 6GB, and 16GB RAM[/b] running at the highest settings at [b]30[/b] frames per second, at [b]1920x1080[/b] resolution. The game is [b]locked[/b] on [b]30 FPS[/b]. If you try to unlock the framerate to 60 or more FPS, the game’s speed will increase, and most of the animations will disappear.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
If you accept the game for what it is, that means a light-hearted fun with unique design rather than a competitive real-time strategy game, then it presents a fair amount of entertainment. Playing all three campaigns in co-op makes it for a better experience. However, the 30 frames per second cap and other aforementioned shortcomings can definitely be a problem for many.

Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3 is a real-time strategy game and obviously the follow-up to Red Alert 2. While I absolutely loved Red Alert 2 I can't say the same for this title.

First, there are some things Red Alert 3 does well. The storyline is as cheesy as it comes and that is what fans expect and love. It is also great that the game has actors like Tim Curry, George Takei and David Hasselhoff, who really seem to enjoy performing the B-movie-like storyline.

However, Red Alert 3 has many problems compared to its predecessor. The units have a cartoonish look to them and look like child's toys. Many of them look so over the top that it is just ridiculous. Also, the weapon's effects and sounds don't convey any impact, further reinforcing that impression.

The gameplay itself comes off as very hectic because units cannot take any damage, no matter the unit type. Even the biggest tanks and ships give off the impression of being made of paper. They get destroyed within seconds leaving no room for actual micromanagement. The problem is that the game wants the player to micromanage since every unit has some sort of special ability. There is not much room to use them however and I would have preferred not having them at all except the toggled abilites. The units' AI is also pretty bad. If the enemy has a slightly longer range they will refrain from retaliating and just get destroyed. Anti-air weaponry is extremely underwhelming in this game. Often building turrets don't seem to make no sense at all. Even if you have a solid turret setup there is just not much use in defending since there are so many units that can destroy your base from huge distances. If the enemy uses aircraft they will still destroy your base because there is no defense that will keep them from destroying at least one target in every run.

Red Alert 3 features a computer controlled partner in every campaign mission. This partner can be replaced by a human player and while I appreciate the idea of making the whole campaign able to be played coop it just doesn't work. The computer partner is highly unreliable in its performance. In some missions it will basically win the mission by itself with you struggling to keep up with the pace and in some missions it will be literally useless. During the last mission of the Rising Sun campaign my AI partner was actually unable to even defend its own base. When I didn't continually sent units there my partner would just be annihilated within a few minutes. All of this while I had my own problems, being hammered by airstrikes, superweapons and ground troops.

The campaign should come with a trigger warning (pun intended) because all missions are heavily built around triggers that you most of the time cannot see coming. However you need to be prepared for them because if you're not you have basically lost. There is no reaction time since the game is fast and units and buildings cannot withstand any damage. It's bad design if you can only win by being able to see into the future. If you have run your head into the wall a few times you will know the triggers and it basically becomes a minigame of avoiding those. One of the worst examples is from the Rising Sun campaign. At one point you will be confronted with a huge enemy fleet and have to hold out until your battleships arrive. When they arrive it is still not enough to destroy the enemie's base but you absolutely need to destroy all their shipyards. Why you ask? Because the AI will start producing an indefinite amount of aircraft carriers and since anti-air turrets are horribly weak you will lose.

Red Alert 3 is not a horrible game but is has so many shortcomings compared to its predecessor that I cannot recommend it at all.

P.S.: If you liked the Tanya from Red Alert 2 you will be severely disappointed.

Command and Conquer 3 is one of the best RTS games you can play today, as it has aged well with time, and the complexity and captivating game play keeps it relevant in today's market. It is an experience unlike any other as it pertains to any and everyone, as the art of war does not discriminate. Command and Conquer 3 has three different campaigns as you explore war through the eyes of the Allies, Soviets, and the Empire of the Rising Sun while dominating your foes and watching those around you become corrupt with power. Command and Conquer’s campaign has elite pacing contrary to other RTS games, as Command and Conquer 3 does not overwhelm the player with everything the game has to offer from the beginning. As the campaign develops, they slowly unravel the more advanced concepts as the player develops the skills needed to conquer their foes, making it beginner-friendly. Additionally, all the new developments do not feel out of place, as they fit well within the story, as the more advanced forms of combat only show up in the late game. Each country has unique tech and concepts tailored to its beliefs and culture, making each campaign dramatically different and forces the player to think on their feet as combat ensues. Outside the campaign, you can enjoy the skirmish mode where you can hone your skills and master the art of war, as Command and Conquer 3 gives you all the tools to make each skirmish tailored to the player's needs. This allows for an infinite amount of possibilities, making it a game you can come back to time and time again and always find something new to enjoy. I would thoroughly recommend this game to anyone who loves RTS games or is looking to get into the RTS genre, as it has something for both veterans and rookies.

I felt like a serious review was needed for this game, since most are either "I hate this, Red Alert 2 is better" or "LoL Tim Curry meme!!!"
This game is likely the best thing EA has made, or is part of an elite group. What's not to love? Graphically, it looks great for 2008, especially the HD cutscenes. The three factions are wacky and rediculous, each made to go with a specific wacky strategy. Each campaign, one for each faction, has an introduction to each faction's units and a funny yet well thought-out story. 
Yes, there is a coop feature, but I never used it. Once, when the service was still up under EA, I tried the coop, and both sides had a unique but well-balanced start.
Back to the cutscenes, they are God's gift to video games. The three faction leaders are well-renowned actors who, luckily, are known for being able to do a not-serious role. George Takei, Tim Curry, and J.K. Simmons all make masterful performances, especially Tim Curry, who is essentially the main character of each story.
Overall, a fantastic game and one worth playing. What are you spending $20 on, Starbucks? Spend it on this.

What is that...? The 2024 Cast of Hollywood's 1st $1 Billion Feature Film...(?) NO! That is the cast of Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3 (2008). Albeit, Kari Wuhrer was not cast in this third Command & Conquer, that cast listed above is still a AAA cast brought together not for a film, but for a video game in a popular RTS franchise...that somehow Electronic Arts managed to ruin in the years since. So, you get all of that acting goodness, PLUS! There's a classic RTS game all assembled in one package - how could I not recommend C&C:Red Alert 3?!
